 Story Highlights
 At the time Princeton Equity Partners bought Five Star Franchising in 2021, Five Star’s brands were Bath Solutions and a digital marketing company called ProNexis. Today it has nine companies. 
 “We felt like there would be some nice investor appetite," said Princeton Equity Managing Partner Doug Kennealey on why now was the right time to sell Five Star. 
 LLCP’s other franchise investments include Shipley Donuts, Kilwins Quality Confections and Synergy HomeCare. 
 The franchisor of Five Star Bath Solutions has a new owner. 
 Princeton Equity Group sold Five Star Franchising to Levine Leichtman Capital Partners after five years backing the portfolio company. 
 “[LLCP] very clearly became, in our minds, the right partner to help us accomplish our vision and take us to this next level,” said Five Star CEO Scott Abbott. “They see how, over the last four or five years, we’ve created value and added value to the brands we have already acquired, and they really want to help us accelerate that.” 
 Scott Abbott is the CEO of Five Star Franchising.
 At the time Princeton bought it in 2021, Five Star’s brands were Bath Solutions and a digital marketing company called ProNexis. Today, Five Star’s other brands are Mosquito  Shield , Decorate With Lights, Card My Yard , Five Star Painting , Five Star Flooring , Bio-One , Gotcha Covered and 1-800-Packouts . The franchises account for more than 970 locations across the United States and Canada.
 Related: Princeton Equity Group Gives Lifeblood to High-growth Founders 
 When Five Star was looking for a buyer several years ago, Princeton stood out because of its commitment to the franchise business model, Abbott said. 
 “We needed to have a partner that could help us accelerate that growth, and we wanted to make sure that we didn’t have to educate our partners on how franchising works and the unique nature of the relationship with franchisors and franchisees, and how to gain alignment,” Abbott said. “They really bought into our vision [which] made them the right candidate.” 
 Princeton Equity Managing Partner Doug Kennealey said the firm was interested in the home services category. 
 “We felt like it was a great place to invest,” he said. “We felt like a lot of the businesses were recession resilient. We felt like there were macro trends in the ‘do-it-for-me’ versus ‘do-it-yourself.’ … We felt like with Scott at the helm [of Five Star], we could create something very special.” 
 Related: Ellie Mental Health to Sell All Corporate Clinics Amid Franchisee Disputes 
 The firm and Five Star "accomplished a lot” in their five years together, Kennealey said, going from a couple brands to nine.  
 With that in mind, now felt like the right time for Princeton to sell. Making that decision with any company is “as much art as it is science,” he said. 
 Doug Kennealey is a managing partner at Princeton Equity Group.
 “We felt like there would be some nice investor appetite, and from a private equity perspective, that’s roughly the time when we target exiting a company,” Kennealey said. “Scott and the management team were on board with it. That’s really important for us. … We really care about when they think the right time is to maybe exit, and we were all aligned on that.” 
 Princeton Equity still owns a number of franchise brands: Barry’s , Amped Fitness, D1 Training , Pirtek USA , Restoration 1, Stretch Zone , Stellar Service Brands, Strickland Brothers Oil Change , Ellie Mental Health and KidStrong . 
 Related: Fitness Franchisor D1 Training Faces Fraud Allegations as Franchisees Say They Were Misled 
 Five Star’s lead financial adviser on this deal was Robert W. Baird & Co. Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld LLP was Princeton and Five Star’s legal counsel for the deal.

 LLCP’s other franchise investments include Shipley Donuts , Kilwins Quality Confections and Synergy HomeCare . 
 As for the future, LLCP Managing Partner Matthew Frankel said Five Star is still on a “strong growth trajectory.” 
 “We look forward to leveraging our extensive experience in the franchising space and working with management to continue to expand unit count, drive strong same-store sales growth, and acquire additional brands,” Frankel said in the press release . 
 Abbott said customers and franchisees can expect more of the same from Five Star. 
 “We’ll continue to build the brands we have, add value to our franchisees, focus on their unit economics,” Abbott said, “and ultimately take that same recipe into other new categories where we feel like they are synergistic with our existing brands and our platform, and finding ways to really create value for our franchise owners.”
